newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen weak despite waning rate fears.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen weak despite waning rate fears.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) and Euroyen futures traded on SIMEX continued their downward trend on Monday, despite the disappearance of recent rumours of an imminent rise in Japanese interest rates.

Dealers said most of the futures market was now convinced there would be no change in Bank of Japan rate policy in the immediate future. But they said the momentum of recent falls had now taken on a life of its own.
"Technically the pattern on Euroyen is now weak," said one Singapore-based floor dealer at a U.S. bank.
Rumours of a rate rise were fed by comments from Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara on November 7 suggesting the Japanese economy was gaining strength.
Although the rumours were officially contradicted later, they persisted for most of the week and helped knock JGBs and Euroyen futures down across the curve.
Dealers said the June Euroyen contract had been fairly quiet for most of Monday. After dipping to an early low of 99.06, the contract had settled back to trade between 99.08 and 99.10.
But they said the direction still appeared to be lower.
"I think the lead June Euroyen contract will be testing the big (99) figure soon," said one dealer.
In late trade, the June 1997 Euroyen contract was down to 99.09 against its IMM close at 99.10 on 11,510 lots.
A chart analyst said the June contract was likely to slip to just under 89.90 if it managed to break the 99.00 figure.
The December JGB futures contract ended 0.29 cents down at 123.51 after hitting an early low of 123.32. Volume was 397 lots.
Brokers said the contract had found little support from investors, who mostly stayed sidelined in the hope of a rally, but had seen some dealer short-covering at around 123.35.
Eurodollar futures were quiet due to the Veteran's Day public holiday in the United States.
The March 1997 Eurodollar contract closed at 94.45, unchanged from its IMM close.
